title: Musicians and Singers
description: Play one or more musical instruments or sing. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for sound or video recording.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Perform before live audiences in concerts, recitals, educational presentations, and other social gatherings.
Sing a cappella or with musical accompaniment.
Interpret or modify music, applying knowledge of harmony, melody, rhythm, and voice production to individualize presentations and maintain audience interest.
Specialize in playing a specific family of instruments or a particular type of music.
Sing as a soloist or as a member of a vocal group.
Observe choral leaders or prompters for cues or directions in vocal presentation.
Memorize musical selections and routines, or sing following printed text, musical notation, or customer instructions.
Play musical instruments as soloists, or as members or guest artists of musical groups such as orchestras, ensembles, or bands.
Play from memory or by following scores.
Provide the musical background for live shows, such as ballets, operas, musical theatre, and cabarets.
Audition for orchestras, bands, or other musical groups.
Make or participate in recordings in music studios.
Make or participate in recordings.
Improvise music during performances.
Perform in television, radio, or movie productions.
Practice singing exercises and study with vocal coaches to develop voice and skills and to rehearse for upcoming roles.
Learn acting, dancing, and other skills required for dramatic singing roles.
Seek out and learn new music suitable for live performance or recording.
Practice performances, individually or in rehearsal with other musicians, to master individual pieces of music or to maintain and improve skills.
Transpose music to alternate keys, or to fit individual styles or purposes.
Compose songs or create vocal arrangements.
Arrange and edit music to fit style and purpose.
Sight-read musical parts during rehearsals.
Listen to recordings to master pieces or to maintain and improve skills.
Research particular roles to find out more about a character, or the time and place in which a piece is set.
Teach music for specific instruments.
Promote their own or their group's music by participating in media interviews and other activities.
Direct bands or orchestras.
Collaborate with a manager or agent who handles administrative details, finds work, and negotiates contracts.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Blogging software, Facebook, Instagram.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: SAP software.

skills.name: Music or sound editing software
skills.def: Software to record or convert analog sounds to a digital format, or to apply effects such as fades, noise filtering, or volume adjustment. Examples: Acoustica Mixcraft, Apple GarageBand, Audacity, Avid Technology Pro Tools.
